comparator.name: International Bachelor Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme overview and 2026-2027 study schedule establish a 180-EC three-year bachelor with broad first- and second-year sequences in economics, business economics and quantitative methods. The third year contains 24 EC of minor/study-abroad/internship and elective space, 2 EC of Career Skills, a 24-EC major and a 10-EC individual thesis. The official major schedule lists nine majors but identifies no default or general route, so this reconstruction preserves the restricted 24-EC major choice generically rather than selecting a route for UCR convenience.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match covers the programme-wide economics, business and empirical core. Accounting was assessed but cannot support a distinct 24-course UCR programme because UCR has only one dedicated accounting course. The behavioural-and-health direction and the financial-economics direction each support coherent, feasible and substantively distinct curricula, so both are included. Markets, organisations and strategy are already substantively covered by the closest-match curriculum. International and policy economics remain defensible directions, but the maximum of three alternatives is reached; urban, port and transport economics is not feasible at UCR because the required specialist domain sequence is absent.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme provides a fixed two-year specialist sequence in economics, business economics and quantitative methods, followed by a formal major, seminar and individual thesis. UCR can build coherent economics-and-business, behavioural-and-health and finance-and-quantitative programmes, but it does not reproduce that full specialist sequence or a dedicated Economics and Business Economics thesis.
